subject: Nanotechnology
title: Nano in Your Phone
description: One-minute skill: Nano in Your Phone.

hook.text: Your smartphone holds billions of transistors smaller than a virus — nanotechnology in your pocket.

buildup.text: Modern chips use 3-nanometer nodes — gates so small that a dozen silicon atoms span them.

discovery.text: At this scale, quantum tunneling causes electrons to leak through barriers that should block them.

twist.text: Engineers fight leakage with new materials and 3D transistor designs — reinventing the chip every year.

climax.text: Without nanotechnology, your phone would be the size of a room and a million times slower.

punchline.text: Billions of nano-switches power every screen tap.

quiz.question: What challenge arises at the 3-nanometer chip node?
options: Quantum tunneling causes electrons to leak through barriers
Transistors become too heavy to fit on a chip
